Outcome:
        VetMedStat consultation Case #12170805-15 for patient BOO CUNNINGHAM 51733320251206 | 517333

         

         

                                                                                     

                    This is your consultation report regarding BOO CUNNINGHAM, Case #12170805-15.

         

                    To view, share, download your report, or submit with a new service, click below:

         

                View Case in VetMedStat

         

         

                        Radiograph ConsultPresenting Complaint: Cardiorespiratory

History: Clinical signs (Coughing, Respiratory distress, Abnormal breathing), History (Yesterday began having increased respiratory rate upwards of 90 brpm with lowest being 50-60 brpm. O notes P would stretch neck out in distress to breathe. P received abx and cerenia inj at rDVM yesterday.Today, P continued to have a respiratory rate of 90, lowest would be 50-60 but no coughing. P was having quick, shallow breaths. O states breathing has been static since yesterday with no decline but no improvement. Episodes of P struggling to breathe have become more prominent per O with an abdominal push consistent since yesterday.Current Medications and last time given: Today: 8 am: prednisone, trazodone (1/2 tab 100 mg) - has been helping a lot for her coughing, 1/2 claritin and hydrocodone, most are BID, doxycycline dose last night and this morning at 8 am(1/4 tab 100 mg)11/25 placed back on pred - was doing well with her coughing, steadily improved, cough subsiding but increased respiratory ratehx collapsing trachea + MMVD B1 + oral mass)

Physical Exam: Summary of PE findings (no ff on pocus diffuse b lines increased )

Diagnostics: Diagnostics (VBG WNL)

Treatment: Tx plan (0.3mg/kg torb)

Clinical Concern/Differentials: Additional medically pertinent information (heart failure vs chronic broncitis vs collaping trachea)

THORAX (December 6, 2025): Left lateral, right lateral and orthogonal radiographs are provided, a total of 3 views. COMPARISON: none.------ FINDINGS:HEART & PULMONARY VASCULATURE: There is the subjective impression of right-sided cardiomegaly, with rounded cranial margins the cardiac silhouette on the lateral images and the impression of a soft tissue bulge from the 6 to 11 o\'clock position on the dorsoventral projection. There is also impression of a soft tissue bulge at the 1 to 2 o\'clock position of the cardiac silhouette on the dorsoventral projection. There is moderate obliquity present on the dorsoventral projection which may influence this appearance. There is suspect dilation of at least one of the cranial lobar pulmonary arteries in relation of the corresponding veins identified on the left lateral projection. Visibility of the lobar pulmonary vasculature is limited due to summation with surrounding pulmonary pathology and further assessment cannot be provided. No abnormalities of the aorta, caudal vena cava, or remaining peripheral vasculature are identified. VHS = 10.3 v, normal being <10.7 in the general canine population.VLAS = 2.0 v, normal being <2.3.LUNGS AND PLEURAL SPACE: There is a diffuse mixed pulmonary pattern characterized by a mild to moderate interstitial pattern with patchy areas of marked interstitial coalescent alveolar pattern in the mid to ventral aspects of the cranial subsegment of left cranial lung lobe, right cranial lung lobe, right middle lung lobe, as well as the dorsal and caudodorsal aspects of the right caudal and to a lesser extent caudal subsegment of left caudal lung lobe. No discrete pulmonary nodules or masses are identified. No abnormalities of the pleural space are identified. All of the provided images are variably expiratory in timing of image acquisition, potentially contributing to the overall increased radiodensity of the lung parenchyma.TRACHEA, UPPER AIRWAY AND LOBAR BRONCHI: There is mild to moderate smoothly marginated ventrally convex soft tissue superimposed with the dorsal aspect of the cervical trachea extending from the mid cervical region to the level of thoracic inlet, with the dorsal tracheal wall remaining well defined. DIAPHRAGM: No abnormalities of the diaphragm are identified. MEDIASTINUM & LYMPH NODES: No intrathoracic lymphadenopathy is identified. No abnormalities of the esophagus are identified. The remaining mediastinal structures are normal. CRANIAL ABDOMEN: The stomach is mildly distended with gas and a small mount of fluid that appropriately change position between images. There is a mild amount of faint mineral opaque material admixed with feces in the ascending colon. On the right lateral projection, there is also the impression of a rectangular/cuboidal shaped soft tissue to faintly mineral opaque structure superimposed with intestine in the cranial abdomen, extending in a cranial and ventral to caudodorsal orientation just caudal to the stomach. This structure is not identified on subsequent images, and is thought most likely to be a normal variant due to superimposition of multiple overlying intestinal segments creating variable mach lines. SKELETAL AND SUPERFICIAL SOFT TISSUES: There are mild osteophytes in the caudal aspect of the humeral heads and glenoids bilaterally.------CONCLUSIONS:1. Mixed diffuse asymmetric pulmonary pattern, as described, predominated by a unstructured interstitial pattern. This is a non-specific finding with differential including pulmonary infiltrate secondary to pulmonary hypertension, fibrosis, interstitial pneumonia, noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, atypical appearance of neoplastic metastasis, and likely a component of physiologic atelectasis. Cardiogenic pulmonary edema is considered given the provided clinical history, though subjectively less likely given the pattern distribution and lack of lobar venous distention and lack of reported coughing episodes. • The ventrally distributed alveolar pattern in the right cranial, middle, and cranial subsegment left cranial lung lobe also warrant consideration for bronchopneumonia. Again however, the lack of coughing episodes (as well as the lack of reported pyrexia) do not support this diagnosis, though these clinical signs could be affected/hidden by concomitant anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial therapy.2. Apparent right ventriculomegaly and main pulmonary tear dilation with possible cranial lobar pulmonary arterial dilation. This combination of radiographic findings is suggestive of underlying pulmonary hypertension with secondary cor pulmonale. The rounded appearance of the cardiac silhouette as well as prominent main pulmonary artery may alternatively be attributable to obliquity on the dorsoventral projection. No radiographic evidence of left atrial enlargement or pulmonary venous distention is identified.3. Convex soft tissue superimpose the dorsal aspect of the cervical trachea. This is often an incidental finding, representing superposition of a redundant dorsal tracheal membrane, though dynamic tracheal collapse (secondary to chondromalacia) is considered given this patient\'s history.4. Unless mineralized material (e.g. bone) is a normal part of this patient\'s diet, the mineral material in the colon is likely an indication of recent dietary indiscretion.5. Mild to moderate bilateral shoulder osteoarthrosis.6. Rectangular shaped mixed soft tissue and mineral opaque structure identified on the right lateral radiograph highly likely represents a normal variant due to superimposition of overlying ribs, intestinal segments, and intestinal content.Summary statement: This is not a straightforward case, and a combination of multiple concomitant upper airway and cardiopulmonary disease processes may be contributing to radiographic and clinical signs.Based on the combination of above described radiographic findings combined with the history of increased respiratory rate/effort without active coughing, pulmonary fibrosis, noncardiogenic pulmonary edema, +/- pulmonary hypertension are given subjective priority, with bronchopneumonia also of increased consideration given the cranial ventral distribution of the alveolar pattern.Cardiogenic pulmonary edema secondary to left-sided congestive heart failure is subjectively considered less likely given current information, though again would be considered if this patient is hypothermic (information not provided in clinical history). RECOMMENDATIONS:Information on provided at primary clinician/clinical request.
This report influenced by synopsis of patient history/clinical information provided. Absent or incomplete patient information may crucially influence interpretation. Clinic Notes / Specifics:

Small Animal Radiographs Request

Is this patient In-Patient or Out-Patient? In-Patient

Where is the patient currently located?: ICU

Pertinent History: Presented in Acute respiratory distress over weekend. Previous radiographs showed a mixed diffuse asymmetric pulmonary pattern with unstructured interstitial pattern as well as an alveolar pattern cranioventrally. Diagnosed with pulmonary hypertension via echocardiogram on monday, echo in november did not have these changes. Blood work indicated moderate-severe inflammation and thus has been treated presumptively as if had bronchopneumonia. Respiratory rate, effort, and lung auscultation have improved significantly since starting sildenafil and unasyn on monday afternoon. Was weaned down to room air overnight.

Precautions: has been oxygen dependent throughout hospitalization, gets anxious and wound up when handled. Ate at 7am -> can go for rads at 1pm
